claim: DNA of mammoth was detected in two short lake sediment cores of the Yamal peninsula, West Siberia, with ages spanning only the past hundreds of years.
source: Using three different approaches on two short lake sediment cores of the Yamal peninsula, West Siberia, with ages spanning only the past hundreds of years, we detect DNA and identified mitochondrial genomes of multiple mammoth and woolly rhinoceros individuals—both species that have been extinct for thousands of years on the mainland.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: Mitochondrial genomes of multiple mammoth individuals were identified in two short lake sediment cores of the Yamal peninsula.
source: Using three different approaches on two short lake sediment cores of the Yamal peninsula, West Siberia, with ages spanning only the past hundreds of years, we detect DNA and identified mitochondrial genomes of multiple mammoth and woolly rhinoceros individuals—both species that have been extinct for thousands of years on the mainland.
evidence: This is supported by the sequencing data and haplogroup analysis presented in the study.

claim: Mitochondrial genomes of multiple woolly rhinoceros individuals were identified in two short lake sediment cores of the Yamal peninsula.

evidence: This is supported by the sequencing data presented in the study.

claim: More than 400,000 reads were detected in one core assigned to extinct Pleistocene megafauna.
source: The occurrence of clearly identifiable aeDNA of extinct Pleistocene megafauna (e.g. >400 K reads in one core) throughout these two short subsurface cores, along with specificities of sedimentology and dating, confirm that processes acting on regional scales, such as extensive permafrost thawing, can influence the aeDNA record and should be accounted for in aeDNA paleoecology.
evidence: This is directly supported by the sequencing data from the study.

claim: Processes acting on regional scales, such as extensive permafrost thawing, can influence the aeDNA record.

claim: Short subsurface sediment cores were retrieved from two Arctic thermokarst lakes (LK-001 and LK-007) on the Yamal peninsula, Siberia, in 2019.

claim: The active thermokarst in the study area likely began during the climatic optimum of the Holocene (9000–3,000 BC).
source: Here, the active thermokarst likely began during the climatic optimum of the Holocene (9000–3,000 BC; Savvichev et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The LK-001 and LK-007 lake basins are interbedded mainly into the IVth marine plain, formed in the Kazantsevskaya, Marine Isotopic Stage 5.
source: The LK-001 and LK-007 lake basins are interbedded mainly into the IVth marine plain, formed in the Kazantsevskaya, Marine Isotopic Stage 5.
evidence: This is geological information about the study site.

claim: The permafrost of these lake catchments was formed no earlier than 70—60 kyr BP after the Kazantsevskaya transgression.
source: The permafrost of these lake catchments was formed no earlier than 70—60 kyr BP after the Kazantsevskaya transgression in more sub-aerial conditions and with mean annual temperatures 6 to 7 °C lower than modern temperatures (Baulin et al., 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The permafrost was formed with mean annual temperatures 6 to 7 °C lower than modern temperatures.
source: The permafrost of these lake catchments was formed no earlier than 70—60 kyr BP after the Kazantsevskaya transgression in more sub-aerial conditions and with mean annual temperatures 6 to 7 °C lower than modern temperatures (Baulin et al., 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The lake basins may be paleo-marine remnants.
source: As this area was under coastal-marine conditions for a long period, these lake basins may be paleo-marine remnants, or they were formed later as a result of thermokarst over the segregated or tabular (massive) ground ice during the Holocene climatic optimum (Kachurin, 1961).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on geological history.

claim: The lake basins may have been formed as a result of thermokarst over the segregated or tabular (massive) ground ice during the Holocene climatic optimum.
source: As this area was under coastal-marine conditions for a long period, these lake basins may be paleo-marine remnants, or they were formed later as a result of thermokarst over the segregated or tabular (massive) ground ice during the Holocene climatic optimum (Kachurin, 1961).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citation.

claim: The area is subject to abrupt permafrost thaw (thermo-denudation), resulting in the formation of retrogressive-thaw slumps (thermocirques).
source: The area is also subject to abrupt permafrost thaw (thermo-denudation), resulting, for example, in the formation of retrogressive-thaw slumps (thermocirques) and the transport of a large amounts of thawed terrestrial material into the lake water (Dvornikov et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Abrupt permafrost thaw results in the transport of large amounts of thawed terrestrial material into the lake water.
source: The area is also subject to abrupt permafrost thaw (thermo-denudation), resulting, for example, in the formation of retrogressive-thaw slumps (thermocirques) and the transport of a large amounts of thawed terrestrial material into the lake water (Dvornikov et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Abrupt permafrost thaw processes normally appear adjacent to lakes and can form thermo-terraces within lake catchments.
source: Such abrupt permafrost thaw processes normally appear adjacent to lakes and can form specific geomorphological elements, that is, thermo-terraces (Kizyakov et al., 2006) within lake catchments and lakes
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Abrupt permafrost thaw processes are normally polycyclic processes appearing due to the extension of a seasonally thawed layer (active layer) up to the top of massive ice.
source: they are normally polycyclic processes appearing due to the extension of a seasonally thawed layer (active layer) up to the top of massive ice and more favorable thermal conditions within the existing forms (Leibman and Kizyakov, 2007; Kokelj et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Traces of past thermo-denudation can be observed within both lake catchments.
source: Traces of past thermo-denudation can be observed within both lake catchments.
evidence: This is an observation from the field study.

claim: In catchments of five neighboring lakes, large retrogressive-thaw slumps appeared in recent years (2012–2013) accompanied by the thaw and lateral transport of modern and Late Pleistocene deposits into lakes.
source: In catchments of five neighboring lakes, large retrogressive-thaw slumps appeared in recent years (2012–2013) accompanied by the thaw and lateral transport of modern and Late Pleistocene deposits into lakes.
evidence: This is an observation from the study area.

claim: The two studied lakes are headwater lakes (with outlet, no apparent inlet).
source: However, the two studied lakes are headwater lakes (with outlet, no apparent inlet) and this option can only be considered in terms of small thermo-erosional valleys within the catchments.
evidence: This is an observation from the field study.

claim: An alternative mechanism for the redistribution of Late Pleistocene material in the sediments is related to subcap methane emission (bubbling) from degrading permafrost beneath the lake bottom.
source: An alternative mechanism for the redistribution of Late Pleistocene material in the sediments is related to subcap methane emission (bubbling) from degrading permafrost beneath the lake bottom.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed by the authors.

claim: In-lake bubbling can be observed in a circum-Arctic scale: in North-East Siberia, Alaska and Canada.
source: In-lake bubbling can be observed in a circum-Arctic scale: in North-East Siberia, Alaska and Canada.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Arctic lake processes.

claim: In-lake bubbling is common especially in lakes with a depth exceeding two meters, which do not freeze entirely up to the bottom in winter, leading to the formation of a talik.
source: This is common especially in lakes with a depth exceeding two meters, which do not freeze entirely up to the bottom in winter, leading to the formation of a talik (a layer of year-round unfrozen ground that lies in permafrost area).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Arctic lake processes.

claim: The expansion of the talik may trigger subcap methane emission, which can reach 40–70 kg yr–1 of pure (94–100%) methane in neighboring lakes.
source: The expansion of the talik may further trigger subcap methane emission, which can reach 40–70 kg yr–1 of pure (94–100%) methane in neighboring lakes (Kazantsev et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Constant methane seepage does not allow ice to be formed in winter and can potentially disturb the stratigraphy of lake sediments.
source: The constant methane seepage does not allow ice to be formed in winter (whereas the normal winter ice thickness is approximately 1.5 m) and can potentially disturb the stratigraphy of lake sediments.
evidence: This is an inference about the effects of methane seepage.

claim: Dramatic emissions of methane can form craters in terrestrial and lacustrine environments.
source: Additionally, dramatic emissions of methane can form craters in terrestrial and lacustrine environments (Dvornikov et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The simultaneous finding of a Pb210 chronology indicating recent sediment deposition and of plant macrofossils that dated to >8000 years BP suggests lateral input of ancient material.
source: In the case reported here, the simultaneous finding of a Pb210 chronology indicating recent sediment deposition and of plant macrofossils that dated to >8000 years BP in a sample from 36.5 cm, suggest lateral input of ancient material, including the mammalian DNA, putatively related to permafrost thawing processes.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of dating results.

claim: The lateral input of ancient material is putatively related to permafrost thawing processes.
source: In the case reported here, the simultaneous finding of a Pb210 chronology indicating recent sediment deposition and of plant macrofossils that dated to >8000 years BP in a sample from 36.5 cm, suggest lateral input of ancient material, including the mammalian DNA, putatively related to permafrost thawing processes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the data and knowledge of local processes.

claim: Numerous studies on aDNA discussed possible leaching through sedimentary strata of the DNA itself, yet it was typically considered not an issue as most of these studies were conducted under stable permafrost or similar conditions.
source: Numerous studies on aDNA discussed possible leaching through sedimentary strata of the DNA itself, yet it was typically considered not an issue as most of these studies were conducted under stable permafrost or similar conditions (e.g. Hansen et al., 2006; Haile et al., 2007, but see Andersen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Permafrost thawing and re-deposition of material adds a new dimension to the problem of temporal interpretation of aeDNA.
source: Permafrost thawing and re-deposition of material adds a new dimension to this problem of temporal interpretation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the findings of the study.

claim: The retrieval of mammoth sequences from both cores of two lakes located approximately 5 km apart suggests that this is not an isolated phenomenon but occurs on a regional or even larger scale.
source: The fact that we retrieved mammoth sequences from both cores of two lakes located approximately 5 km apart suggests that this is not an isolated phenomenon but occurs on a regional or even larger scale.
evidence: This is inferred from the data from both lakes.

claim: Abrupt permafrost thaw processes are widespread in the Arctic plains (West Siberia, Taimyr, Chukotka, Alaska, Canadian Arctic).
source: Given the wide spread of abrupt permafrost thaw processes in the Arctic plains (West Siberia, Taimyr, Chukotka, Alaska, Canadian Arctic; Kizyakov et al., 2006 and references therein), the phenomena of disturbed stratigraphy of lacustrine sediments can potentially be observed at a pan-Arctic scale.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The phenomena of disturbed stratigraphy of lacustrine sediments can potentially be observed at a pan-Arctic scale.
source: Given the wide spread of abrupt permafrost thaw processes in the Arctic plains (West Siberia, Taimyr, Chukotka, Alaska, Canadian Arctic; Kizyakov et al., 2006 and references therein), the phenomena of disturbed stratigraphy of lacustrine sediments can potentially be observed at a pan-Arctic scale.
evidence: This is inferred from the widespread nature of permafrost thaw processes.

claim: Temporal interpretation of sedimentary aeDNA records should be exercised with caution.
source: While this indicates that temporal interpretation of sedimentary aeDNA records should be exercised with caution, our study also demonstrates that a careful evaluation of available information on the site and ecosystem in conjunction with the use of independent dating techniques can uncover incongruencies.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the findings of the study.

claim: A careful evaluation of available information on the site and ecosystem in conjunction with the use of independent dating techniques can uncover incongruencies in aeDNA records.
source: While this indicates that temporal interpretation of sedimentary aeDNA records should be exercised with caution, our study also demonstrates that a careful evaluation of available information on the site and ecosystem in conjunction with the use of independent dating techniques can uncover incongruencies.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the methods and findings of the study.

claim: Artefactual stratigraphies caused by equivalent processes acting for a limited time will not be detected as easily in older time periods as in the case of long extinct species.
source: This is more difficult in older time periods, where artefactual stratigraphies caused by equivalent processes acting for a limited time will not be detected as easily as in our case of long extinct species.
evidence: This is an inference about the challenges of detecting such processes in different contexts.

claim: The inclusion of robust dating techniques and knowledge of local geophysical processes can provide good arguments to evaluate the reliability of aeDNA records.
source: However, we suggest that the inclusion of robust dating techniques and knowledge of local geophysical processes can provide good arguments to evaluate the reliability of aeDNA records.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's approach and findings.

claim: Sediment cores were retrieved using a UWITEC piston corer.
source: In 2019, sediment cores (6 cm diameter; Table 1) were retrieved from two lakes (LK-001 and LK-007, respectively, Table 1) on the Yamal peninsula, Siberia, using a UWITEC piston corer (UWITEC, Mondsee, Austria).
evidence: This describes the field methodology.

claim: The sediment cores had a diameter of 6 cm.
source: In 2019, sediment cores (6 cm diameter; Table 1) were retrieved from two lakes (LK-001 and LK-007, respectively, Table 1) on the Yamal peninsula, Siberia, using a UWITEC piston corer (UWITEC, Mondsee, Austria).
evidence: This describes the field methodology.

claim: Radiometric dating from 0 to 39.5 cm depth was performed at the Environmental Radioactivity Research Centre, University of Liverpool.
source: from lake LK-001, a secondary core was taken which was sliced in the field at 1 cm steps for radiometric dating from 0 to 39.5 cm depth, performed at the Environmental Radioactivity Research Centre, University of Liverpool (Supplement section 9).
evidence: This describes where the dating analysis was performed.

claim: 14C dating of three specimens of plant remains was performed at depths of 36.5 cm, 51 cm, and 74 cm.
source: Additional 14 C dating of three specimens of plant remains, extracted at 36.5 cm, 51 cm, and 74 cm, was performed (Supplement section 9).
evidence: This describes the radiocarbon dating methodology.

claim: DNA was isolated from 16 samples of core LK-007.
source: Sedimentary DNA was isolated from 23 samples of core LK-001 and from 16 samples of core LK-007 using commercially available kits with modified protocols (Supplement section 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedures.

claim: Enrichment probes were designed from mitogenomes of 17 herbivorous mammal species that currently or previously occurred in the Arctic.
source: Enrichment probes were designed from mitogenomes of 17 herbivorous mammal species that currently or previously occurred in the Arctic (Appendix 1—table 2) and few lichen sequences (Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: This describes the probe design methodology.

claim: Reads assigned to Coelodonta antiquitatis were mapped to the NCBI reference mitogenome NC_012681.1.
source: reads assigned to Coelodonta antiquitatis were mapped to the NCBI reference mitogenome NC_012681.1 2.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatic analysis methodology.

claim: The reads mapped to mammoth from the top three libraries were assigned to haplogroup using mixemt with a custom-made representative panel of 15 mammoth mitogenomes.
source: The reads mapped to mammoth from the top three libraries were assigned to haplogroup using mixemt (https://github.com/svohr/mixemt, Copy archieved at Vohr, 2024) with a custom-made representative panel of 15 mammoth mitogenomes (Figure 2; Appendix 1—table 6).
evidence: This describes the haplogroup analysis methodology.

claim: Mammal metabarcoding PCRs were performed on 21 DNA extracts of core LK-001 and 27 samples of core LK-007, with eight independent replicates each.
source: Mammal metabarcoding PCRs were performed on 21 DNA extracts of core LK-001 and 27 samples of core LK-007, with eight independent replicates, each.
evidence: This describes the metabarcoding methodology.

claim: Human blocking primers were included in the metabarcoding PCRs.
source: Established metabarcoding primers were used (Giguet-Covex et al., 2014), and human blocking primers (Garcés-Pastor et al., 2021) were included.
evidence: This describes the metabarcoding methodology.

claim: Sequencing was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq platform, with 2x150 reads.
source: Sequencing was performed on an Illumina NovaSeq platform, with 2x150 reads.
evidence: This describes the sequencing methodology.

claim: ddPCR was performed with 24 extracts of core LK-001 and with 30 extracts of core LK-007, with three replicates each.
source: With this probe, ddPCR was performed with 24 extracts of core LK-001 and with 30 extracts of core LK-007, with three replicates, each (Supplement section 8).
evidence: This describes the ddPCR methodology.
